criteria_location: Position Statement, pp.1-3 only. Opens with a Certificate of Medical Necessity (CMN) submission note, then adult indications, pediatric indications, retransplant, catch-all investigational sentence, and a contraindications list. Billing/Coding lists only 3 CPT codes; Other (pp.4-5) is Florida organ-transplant statutes, not criteria.
procedures_covered: Heart transplant (CPT 33945), donor cardiectomy (33940), backbench prep (33944)
Heart retransplantation after failed primary transplant

logic.top_level: pathways: separate Adult and Pediatric lists, each 'Accepted indications' (strong) and for adults also 'Probable indications'; each list is an OR of numbered items, some items contain a nested any-of bullet list
logic.exclusions_or_contraindications: Separate trailing list: 'Potential contraindications to cardiac transplantation (subject to the judgment of the transplant center) include:' nine bullets, e.g. 'Known current malignancy, including metastatic cancer'. Not stated as hard NOT; defers to transplant center judgment. Plus catch-all 'considered experimental or investigational in all other situations'.
logic.initial_vs_repeat: 'Heart retransplantation after a failed primary cardiac transplant meets the definition of medical necessity in individuals who meet criteria for heart transplantation.' (reuses the same criteria)

and_or_ambiguity.quote: 1. Hemodynamic compromise due to heart failure demonstrated by any of the following: ... Documented dependence on intravenous inotropic support to maintain adequate organ perfusion, OR
and_or_ambiguity.why_ambiguous: The trailing OR sits at the end of the third sub-bullet but joins item 1 to item 2; sub-bullets themselves carry no OR (the 'any of the following' header supplies it). A parser reading 'OR' as belonging to the last bullet would mis-nest.

and_or_ambiguity.quote: Accepted indications ... Probable indications for cardiac transplantation:
and_or_ambiguity.why_ambiguous: Two tiers ('accepted' vs 'probable') with identical medical-necessity header 'when selection criteria are met'; the text never says whether 'probable' alone suffices for approval.

and_or_ambiguity.quote: Pediatric heart disease with symptoms of heart failure who do not meet the above criteria but who have:
and_or_ambiguity.why_ambiguous: Item 2 is conditional on NOT meeting item 1 (a hidden NOT), then an OR list of seven alternatives.

vague_terms.problem: Refers to criteria below without saying which tier (accepted vs probable) satisfies it.

extraction_hazards: Bullets are either the private-use character U+F0B7 or U+2022 depending on the document (the fusion guideline uses both), never '-' or '*'; nested bullets use other glyphs ('o') or only deeper indentation
Hyperlink navigation bar after the disclaimer is flattened into a 2-3 row text block that looks like headings
Form-feed (\f) page breaks can fall mid-list or immediately before a section heading, so '^HEADING' regexes can miss; no running headers/footers or page numbers to strip
Pediatric bullet list splits across a page break (page 2 to page 3): the last bullet starts a new page after a form feed
CMN instructions use a numbered 1-3 list that is not criteria and is inside the Position Statement
Section heading 'REIMBURSEMENT INFORMATION' has no trailing colon here (others do)
interesting_structures: Two evidence tiers: 'Accepted' vs 'Probable' indications (graded recommendation, not both required)
Contraindications are advisory ('potential', 'subject to the judgment of the transplant center'), so a NOT node would be wrongly hard
Statutory text in OTHER section is not criteria but is long and could be mistaken for it
Hidden NOT in pediatric item 2 ('do not meet the above criteria but who have')

fit_to_tree.scale: 1 = all/any/not expresses it cleanly ... 5 = needs new constructs or human judgment
fit_to_tree.why: Adult/pediatric accepted lists are clean any-of trees with numeric VO2 leaves, but 'probable' tier, advisory contraindications and CMN submission are not plain all/any/not; many leaves ('refractory', 'severe') need clinician judgment.
